jane: Quick heads-up — after quantizing magnet16k to int8 and enabling longctx=65536 I see output divergence compared to fp16 around token ~12k. Short repro and logs below, wondering if this is RoPE scaling or a KV index off-by-one.

jane: Repro steps:
```
# checkout branch: quant-int8-longctx
./run_eval.sh --model magnet16k --quant int8 --context 65536 --prompt-file tests/long_qa.txt --seed 42
```
Outputs diverge (different tokens) after ~12.3k tokens in the same prompt set.

oli: Hmm — do you see drift in hidden states or just final token probs? can you paste the log snippet where it first mismatches?

jane: Pasted extract:
```
[12:18:02] token_idx=12291 ref_prob=0.0034 int8_prob=0.0011 top3_ref=["the","a","it"] top3_int8=["the","it","an"]
[12:18:04] token_idx=12292 ref_tok="company" int8_tok="companies"
```
Seems like probability mass shifts and then alt token picked.

sasha: Could be rope phase scaling + quantization noise accumulating in KV cache. Did you check rotary frequency normalization? We had a mismatch earlier when we rolled the phase-mapping change.

maya: Also confirm whether prefill vs streaming path differs; we saw index skew in streaming prefill with int8 in a past bug. Which codepath did you run?

jane: This was full prefill (single request) — not streaming. I tried with --stream=false explicitly.

sasha: OK — two hypotheses: 1) quantization rounding in qkv matmul cascades with RoPE causing phase amplitude errors; 2) KV store write order or alignment for long windows over ~12k boundary causing fp vs int8 indexing mismatch.

oli: Can you run a small diagnostic that compares rotary-embedding dot products at several positions (fp16 vs int8) and dump KV keys for the indices near 12280-12295? Something like:
```
python - <<PY
from model import Model
m_fp = Model('magnet16k', quant=None)
m_i8 = Model('magnet16k', quant='int8')
for pos in [12275,12280,12285,12290,12295]:
    print(pos, m_fp.rope_cos(pos)[:6], m_i8.rope_cos(pos)[:6])
    print('kv_key_fp', m_fp.kv.dump_key(pos)[:8])
    print('kv_key_i8', m_i8.kv.dump_key(pos)[:8])
PY
```
This will show whether RK alignment differs.

jane: Running that now. Also noticed higher memory spill rates in int8 run: OOMs on smaller hosts, but main test succeeded. Will post output.

ci-bot: CI job quant-longctx-magnet16k triggered: https://ci.redwood/quant-longctx/3456 — started by jane

jane: Diagnostic output (trimmed):
```
12275 fp_cos: [0.982, 0.174, ...] i8_cos: [0.981, 0.174, ...]
kv_key_fp: 0x9af1c3d2 kv_key_i8: 0x9af1c3d2
12290 fp_cos: [0.867, 0.496, ...] i8_cos: [0.862, 0.501, ...]
kv_key_fp: 0x7b4ee11a kv_key_i8: 0x7b4ee11a
```
So keys match at those positions. Small numeric delta in cos values at later positions (12290).

maya: Numeric deltas look small, but with RoPE exponentials / phase wraps even small drift can flip token argmax downstream. Can you re-run with deterministic rounding or higher-precision accumulation in the int8 path to test sensitivity?

jane: Good idea. I recompiled the int8 matmul with accumulation in fp32 (instead of fp16 acc) and re-ran. Divergence pushed out to ~19k tokens (so improved but not fixed).

sasha: That suggests quant accumulation error is a major contributor. If increasing accumulator precision moves the divergence boundary, we can prioritize improving int8 accumulation or applying compensated summation for qkv matmul.

oli: Also we should baseline against a quant-aware RoPE rescale: there's an option to clamp rotary factors per-layer to reduce amplification. Try enabling rope_clamp=0.999 for later layers and re-run a short job.

jane: Will spin both tests (fp32-accum vs rope_clamp). ETA ~30m for small sample.

oli: For the eval harness, capture per-token KL divergence between fp16 and int8; that'll help quantify regression and we can plot drift over token index. Small script idea:
```
compute_kl.py --ref fp16_run.json --target int8_run.json --out kl_by_token.csv
```
We should add this to the nightly quant-bench suite.

maya: Agree. Also add a targeted benchmark: 5 prompts each ~30k tokens to stress long-window. We'll need to ensure prefill GC doesn't prune earlier prefixes.

jane: Update — fp32-accum run shifted mismatch to 19127, rope_clamp run shifted to 15040. I pushed both run artifacts to S3 (s3://redwood-qa/quant-longctx/1768123456/).

sasha: Nice. Priorities: short-term — enable fp32 accumulation in int8 builds for magnet16k. Medium — evaluate rope_clamp defaulting on quantized models where longctx>32k. Long-term — look at per-layer quantization sensitivity and improved quant-aware RoPE parameterization.

oli: I'll open a follow-up RFC/issue with proposed change list and perf impact estimate. Jane — can you attach the KL-by-token CSV when your compute_kl job finishes?

jane: Will do. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

oli: Tagging @infra on infra ramifications for fp32-accum perf cost on Dedicated nodes.

ci-bot: Job quant-longctx-magnet16k completed: SUCCESS (duration 26m)

maya: Small note — if we flip accum to fp32 by default we should add a smoke test to catch regressions in latency-sensitive endpoints.

jane: Agreed. I'll put together a short PR with toggles and a unit test for the rope_cos delta threshold.

sasha: Great thread. Follow-up: sync tomorrow 10am to triage and assign owners.
